title: Saying no: negation
description: Say that something is not so, is not there, did not happen, is not wanted or must not be done.

guide.title: illa and alla
guide.text:
ಇಲ್ಲ (illa) is the negative of iru, 'to be (somewhere), to exist'. It says that something or someone is not present or does not exist, and it is the same for every person: naanu illa, avaru illa, neeru illa.

ಅಲ್ಲ (alla) is the negative of the verbless 'X is Y' sentence. It says that something is not what was claimed: naanu daaktar alla, 'I am not a doctor'; idu sari alla, 'this is not right'.

A quick test: if the positive sentence would use ide / iddaare, the negative is illa. If the positive sentence has no verb, the negative is alla.

With question-word + -oo, a negative gives 'nobody, nothing, nowhere': yaaroo illa (nobody is here), enoo illa (there is nothing), elloo illa (it is nowhere).

examples.english: He / She is not at home.

guide.title: Negating a verb: -alla and -alilla
guide.text:
Negative verbs are wonderfully simple in spoken Kannada, because they do not change with the person.

Don't / doesn't / won't: verb stem + -alla. maadu - ಮಾಡಲ್ಲ (maadalla), hogu - ಹೋಗಲ್ಲ (hogalla), baa - ಬರಲ್ಲ (baralla), tinnu - ತಿನ್ನಲ್ಲ (tinnalla), kudi - ಕುಡಿಯಲ್ಲ (kudiyalla), nodu - ನೋಡಲ್ಲ (nodalla), kelu - ಕೇಳಲ್ಲ (kelalla), kodu - ಕೊಡಲ್ಲ (kodalla), iru - ಇರಲ್ಲ (iralla), aagu - ಆಗಲ್ಲ (aagalla). naanu baralla, avanu baralla, avaru baralla: I, he, they won't come. The written form is the verbal noun + illa: maaduvudilla, baruvudilla.

Didn't: verb stem + -alilla (the infinitive in -alu plus illa). ಮಾಡಲಿಲ್ಲ (maadalilla), ಹೋಗಲಿಲ್ಲ (hogalilla), ಬರಲಿಲ್ಲ (baralilla), ತಿನ್ನಲಿಲ್ಲ (tinnalilla), ಕೊಡಲಿಲ್ಲ (kodalilla), ಆಗಲಿಲ್ಲ (aagalilla). Again one form for all persons. In fast speech the a drops: maadlilla, barlilla.

Isn't / aren't ...-ing: stem + -tilla. ಬರ್ತಿಲ್ಲ (bartilla) is not coming; ಮಾಡ್ತಿಲ್ಲ (maadtilla) is not doing; ಆಗ್ತಿಲ್ಲ (aagtilla) is not happening.

guide.title: Don't! and must not
guide.text:
A negative command is the verb stem + -a + ಬೇಡ (beda): ಹೋಗಬೇಡ (hogabeda), 'don't go', to a friend or child. For the polite form add -i: ಹೋಗಬೇಡಿ (hogabedi). Likewise maadabedi (don't do), barabedi (don't come), mareyabedi (don't forget).

A rule or prohibition - 'one must not, it is not allowed' - uses stem + -a + ಬಾರದು (baaradu): illi nillisabaaradu, 'one must not stop here'. This is what you see on signs.

In fast speech the linking a is dropped: hogbedi, maadbedi, maadbaardu.

examples.english: Don't go. (to a friend or child)

guide.title: Negatives of want, know, like and can
guide.text:
Several everyday words have their own negative partner:

ಬೇಕು (beku) want/need - ಬೇಡ (beda) don't want.
ಗೊತ್ತು (gottu) know - ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ (gottilla) don't know.
ಇಷ್ಟ (ishta) like - ಇಷ್ಟ ಇಲ್ಲ (ishta illa) don't like.
ಬರುತ್ತೆ (barutte) 'comes' = know how to - ಬರಲ್ಲ (baralla) can't, don't know how.
ಆಗುತ್ತೆ (aagutte) 'happens' = is possible - ಆಗಲ್ಲ (aagalla) can't be done, not possible.
ಸಾಕು (saaku) enough - ಸಾಲಲ್ಲ (saalalla) not enough.

All of these take the person in the dative: nanage beda, nanage gottilla, nanage baralla.

phrases.note: illa is the same for every person.
alla, not illa: you are denying what you are.
To a friend or child: hogabeda (ಹೋಗಬೇಡ).
gaadi is any vehicle. -baaradu states a rule.
A language 'comes to you' in Kannada.
